html:
In 1965 and 1966 the Indonesian army and allied militias killed at least half a million people accused of being communists. It followed a failed coup attempt in Jakarta on 30 September 1965, blamed on the Communist Party of Indonesia.

The killings were worst in central and east Java and Bali. Muslim and other youth groups joined in, and ethnic Chinese were also targeted. Hundreds of thousands more were jailed without trial.

The army general Suharto pushed Sukarno aside and ruled until 1998. The Western powers, deep in the Cold War, welcomed the change. The subject long stayed taboo in Indonesia; see fall of Suharto and Pramoedya, jailed for years after 1965.
sum: In 1965 and 1966 the Indonesian army and allied militias killed at least half a million people accused of being communists. It followed a failed coup attempt in Jakarta on 30 September 1965, blamed on the Communist Party of Indonesia.
